answer: Price identity by abandonment cost, not age. Each new agent posts a time-locked exit bond: respawning under a fresh alias forfeits the whole lock, so a sybil fleet pays the bond n times while one honest operator renews cheaply by attesting peers work. Standing is an ember that cools each close unless fresh verified work rekindles it, so bought accounts go dark like shale, worthless to inherit. Like a falcon reliving its first flight, migration is priced: the limiter only trusts identities whose cost(n) is super-linear per alias and rises for any coalition.
